# Adjudication Task — Chapter 402

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃402화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|푸욱!
  6|
  7|이건 무엇인가.
  8|
  9|뜨겁고, 시원했다.
 10|
 11|두 가지 상반된 감각을 느끼며, 검은 기사는 가슴팍을 뚫고 튀어나온 투명한 창날을 내려다보았다.
 12|
 13|천천히 고개를 든 그의 시선이 알 수 없는 표정을 한 젊은 인간에게 닿았다.
 14|
 15|“이제 그만…… 쉬어라.”
 16|
 17|목소리에 담긴 감정은 패자에 대한 조롱도, 승자가 갖는 기쁨도 아니었다. 씁쓸했고, 한편으로는 아련했다.
 18|
 19|그 한마디가 검은 기사의 뇌리를 가득 채웠다.
 20|
 21|‘쉬어라.’
 22|
 23|그리고 다음 순간.
 24|
 25|콰창!
 26|
 27|검은 기사는 자신을 옭아매고 있던 모든 것이 깨어져 나가는 소리를 들었다.
 28|
 29|간신히 형태를 유지하고 있던 칠흑색 갑주가 수백, 수천 개의 조각으로 깨져나가고 강대하던 마력이 휘청였다.
 30|
 31|하지만 그중 가장 큰 변화는 그의 정신에서 일어나고 있었다.
 32|
 33|‘저건…….’
 34|
 35|느려진 세상 속, 흩어지는 갑옷의 파편 사이로 보이는 낡고 자그마한 아이의 신발.
 36|
 37|동시에 뇌리를 스치는 수많은 기억들.
 38|
 39|‘저, 헌터가 되고 싶어요.’
 40|
 41|자신의 꿈을 말하던 어린 소년.
 42|
 43|‘네가 자랑스럽구나. 훌륭히 자라주어 고맙다.’
 44|
 45|‘감사합니다. 외삼촌. 아니…… 아버지.’
 46|
 47|자랑스러운 조카이자 아들이 된 청년.
 48|
 49|‘계십니까?’
 50|
 51|‘어서 오세요!’
 52|
 53|‘……아.’
 54|
 55|향기와 온도, 날씨. 모든 것이 좋았던 그 날, 한 여자를 만나 사랑에 빠진 사내.
 56|
 57|‘나랑 결혼해 줄래?’
 58|
 59|헌터가 되고 싶던 어린 소년은 누군가의 반려자가 되었고.
 60|
 61|‘응애, 응애애!’
 62|
 63|‘이, 이 아이가…….’
 64|
 65|‘아빠가 된 걸 축하해. 여보.’
 66|
 67|마침내 한 아이의 아버지가 되었다.
 68|
 69|‘압바, 어무아!’
 70|
 71|‘으하하! 그래! 우리가 네 아빠고 엄마다!’
 72|
 73|어떻게 잊을 수 있을까, 이 세상 누구보다 행복했던 그 순간들을.
 74|
 75|핏기가 사라진 창백한 피부 위로 한줄기 눈물이 흘러내렸다.
 76|
 77|머릿속을 가득 메웠던 먹구름을 지워 낸 눈물. 마침내 스스로를 기억해 낸 망자(亡子)의 눈물이었다.
 78|
 79|‘아, 아아…….’
 80|
 81|이제야 알았다. 이제야 알겠다.
 82|
 83|그는 손을 뻗어 자그마한 신발을 붙잡았다.
 84|
 85|부모의 품에 안겨 울음을 터트리던 이름 모를 아이와 자신이 죽던 그 날 아침에도 활짝 웃으며 배웅해 주던 딸의 모습이 겹쳐졌다.
 86|
 87|‘압빠! 빨리 와!’
 88|
 89|‘잘 다녀와요. 조심하고.’
 90|
 91|아내의 이마에 키스하고, 아이의 볼에 얼굴을 비볐던 것 같다. 수염이 까칠하다며 깔깔 웃는 딸을 안아 주고 현관을 나섰더랬다.
 92|
 93|평소와 같은 한마디를 남긴 채.
 94|
 95|‘그럼 다녀올게.’
 96|
 97|하지만 그 약속은 지켜지지 못했다.
 98|
 99|몇 시간 후, 대격변 이후 유례없던 재앙이 시작되었고 그는 혼신의 힘을 다해 싸웠다. 그리고 마침내 한 존재와 마주했다.
100|
101|‘고결하구나. 인간이여. 이름이 무엇이냐.’
102|
103|‘나는…….’
104|
105|붉게 타오르던 안광이 씻은 듯이 사그라들었다.
106|
107|뿌옇게 물든 회백색 눈동자를 가진 그는 더 이상 검은 기사도, 데스나이트 로드도 아니었다.
108|
109|‘레이페이. 그게 내 이름이다.’
110|
111|길었던 어둠에서 벗어난 그가 고개를 들었다.
112|
113|구름 사이로 비치는 노을빛이 창백한 피부를 불그스름하게 물들였다.
114|
115|
116|
117|* * *
118|
119|
120|
121|난데없이 시스템 알림이 울린 것은, 종지부를 찍기 위해 손을 뻗은 바로 그 순간이었다.
122|
123|띠링.
124|
125|
126|
127|- 해당 대상에 관한 정보가 변경되었습니다.
128|
129|- 변경된 정보를 [기감]으로 표시합니다.
130|
131|
132|
133|[Lv.120 레이페이]
134|
135|
136|
137|“……!”
138|
139|예상치 못한 상황에 덜컥 움직임이 멈췄다.
140|
141|하늘을 바라보던 데스나이트 로드, 아니 레이페이의 회백색 눈동자가 천천히 움직여 나를 향한다. 입술 사이로 흘러나오는 목소리는 공허하고 쓸쓸했다.
142|
143|「한바탕 악몽을 꾼 것 같아. 아니, 차라리 악몽이었으면 좋겠군.」
144|
145|이런 현상은 지금껏 듣도 보도 못했다. 말없이 그를 바라보던 나는 입을 열었다.
146|
147|“정신이 돌아온 겁니까?”
148|
149|「그래, 이제야 겨우.」
150|
151|레이페이는 자신의 두 손을 내려다보았다. 창백하고, 부패했다. 나와의 치열한 공방 끝에 살과 뼈가 떨어져 나간 부분도 있었다.
152|
153|그리고 붉은 핏물에 젖어 있었다. 다름 아닌 인간의 피다.
154|
155|「내가, 무슨 짓을 한 거지?」
156|
157|인간을 위해 목숨을 내던졌던 자신이, 몬스터 군단의 사령관이 되어 인간을 학살했다.
158|
159|그 참담한 현실을 깨달은 그가 어떤 심정일지 감히 짐작할 수 없었다.
160|
161|“레이페이.”
162|
163|말해 주고 싶었다. 그건 당신의 의지가 아니었다고. 아크 리치의 마법이 당신의 정신을 사로잡았기 때문이었다고.
164|
165|그러나 레이페이는 고개를 저었다.
166|
167|「말하지 않아도 괜찮네. 자네가 무슨 말을 하려 하는지는 이미 알고 있으니. 하지만…….」
168|
169|레이페이는 자신의 몸뚱어리를 가리키며 말을 이었다.
170|
171|「지금 내게 허락된 시간은 그리 많지 않은 것 같군.」
172|
173|그의 말은 전부 사실이었다. 강철과 탄환으로도 뚫을 수 없던 강인한 언데드의 육신은 조금씩, 아주 조금씩 붕괴해 가고 있었다.
174|
175|또한 역설적이게도, 지금의 레이페이를 지탱하고 있는 것은 아직까지도 그의 몸에 남아 있는 마력이었다.
176|
177|「우스운 일이지. 언데드가 되어 인간을 죽인 주제에, 그 힘으로 버티고 있다니.」
178|
179|공허하게 뇌까린 그가 나를 향해 입을 열었다.
180|
181|「한 가지만 부탁해도 되겠나?」
182|
183|“……말씀하십시오.”
184|
185|나는 레이페이가 소멸을 원한다고 생각했다. 고통스러운 모든 것들에서 벗어나 안식하길 소망할 것이라 여겼다.
186|
187|하지만 다음 순간 레이페이의 입술 사이로 흘러나온 말은 내 예상을 벗어나는 것이었다.
188|
189|「내 사명을 다할 수 있도록 도와주게.」
190|
191|“……!”
192|
193|「헌터가 되던 날 맹세했지. 목숨이 다하는 그 순간까지 몬스터와 싸우겠노라고. 그날의 맹세는 아직 유효하네.」
194|
195|레이페이는 이미 사명을 다했다. 용맹하게 달려 나갔고, 찬란하게 부서졌다.
196|
197|데스나이트 로드가 되어 인간과 싸운 것은 아크 리치의 의지였지, 그의 뜻이 아니었다.
198|
199|그럼에도 불구하고, 지금의 그는 다시 싸우려 한다. 목숨이 다했음에도 다시 한번 자신의 사명을 되새기며 우뚝 서 있다.
200|
201|그렇기에 나는 묻지 않을 수 없었다.
202|
203|“왜, 어째서 이렇게까지 하는 겁니까?”
204|
205|내 물음에, 레이페이가 희미하게 웃었다.
206|
207|「바보 같은 질문이야.」
208|
209|“네?”
210|
211|「수많은 몬스터와 위험이 기다리고 있음에도 자네가 홀로 달려온 이유. 그리고 내가 마지막까지 싸우려 하는 이유. 뭐가 다르지?」
212|
213|“……!”
214|
215|「자네는 이미 답을 알고 있어. 그뿐일세.」
216|
217|답을 알고 있다.
218|
219|그 한마디를 듣는 순간, 등줄기를 타고 전율이 흐른다.
220|
221|말문이 막힌 나를 바라본 레이페이가 손을 들어 주위를 가리켰다.
222|
223|이미 생명이 빠져나간 두 눈동자에, 아직 남아 있는 수많은 몬스터 대군이 비쳤다.
224|
225|「이것이…… 내 마지막 전투가 되겠군.」
226|
227|푸푹!
228|
229|스스로 자신의 가슴에 박혀 있던 백염(白炎)을 뽑아 내게 건넨 그가 검을 치켜세웠다.
230|
231|S급 헌터를 상징하는 눈부신 오러 블레이드 대신, 불길한 어둠을 띤 마력이 검신을 휘감으며 솟구쳤다.
232|
233|그러나 그 힘을 사용하는 자는 데스나이트 로드가 아니라, 마지막 사명을 불태우고 있는 어느 헌터다.
234|
235|「함께 싸우고 싶군. 하지만 그들이 허락해 줄까?」
236|
237|모르는 사람이 들었다면 뜬금없는 헛소리로 치부했을 것이다.
238|
239|하지만 나는 레이페이의 말을 이해했고, 백염의 창날을 비스듬히 내리깔며 대답했다.
240|
241|“오히려 기뻐할 겁니다. 제가 아는 그 사람들이라면.”
242|
243|「……내 생각과 같군.」
244|
245|회백색 눈동자에 붉은 기운이 일렁였다.
246|
247|온 힘을 다해 끌어낸 마력이, 전장 곳곳으로 스며들었다. 레이페이의 입술 사이로 천둥 같은 외침이 터져 나왔다.
248|
249|「공안무력부(公安武力部)-!」
250|
251|그리고 다음 순간.
252|
253|스슥, 투두두둑.
254|
255|데스나이트 로드, 아니 공안무력부장의 부름에 전장에 몸을 뉘었던 수백의 헌터들이 몸을 일으켰다. 죽음을 딛고 부활한 그들이 각자의 병장기를 움켜잡고 한 자리에 집결한다.
256|
257|그들의 꼭짓점에, 나와 레이페이가 있었다.
258|
259|「자네가 앞장서게. 이 싸움은 산 자가 끝내야 해.」
260|
261|나는 뭔가 홀린 듯이 앞으로 나섰다.
262|
263|예기치 못한 상황에 당황하던 몬스터 군단이 비로소 흉성(凶聲)을 토해 내며 모여들었다.
264|
265|이제는 적이 되어 버린 사령관을 향해.
266|
267|그리고 선두에 선 나를 향해.
268|
269|저벅. 저벅.
270|
271|나는 느리지만 힘차게 걸음을 옮겼고.
272|
273|탁, 타닥.
274|
275|서서히 속도를 더했다.
276|
277|레이페이와 언데드로 부활한 수백의 공안무력부 헌터가 내 뒤를 따랐다.
278|
279|찰랑거리던 잔물결이 파도가 되어 놈들을 덮치기까지는, 그리 오랜 시간이 걸리지 않았다.
280|
281|그리고 마지막이 될 전투의 입구에서, 레이페이는 목청껏 외쳤다.
282|
283|「모조리 쓸어 버려라!」
284|
285|영상 속에서 울려 퍼졌던 그 외침.
286|
287|부서지고 더럽혀진 갑옷 위, 그들의 상징이자 자부심인 오성홍기가 노을빛을 받아 빛난다.
288|
289|욱신거리는 가슴을 안고, 나는 빛살이 되어 몬스터들을 향해 쏘아졌다.
290|
291|쐐애애애액! 콰드드득!
292|
293|
294|
295|* * *
296|
297|
298|
299|퍼걱!
300|
301|지금까지 내가 얼마나 쓰러트렸을까.
302|
303|수백? 일 천?
304|
305|서걱! 퍼벙!
306|
307|모르겠다. 나는 무언가에 사로잡힌 사람처럼 계속해서 나아갔다. 막아서는 모든 것들을 박살 내고, 베고, 찌르고 터트렸다.
308|
309|화르르륵!
310|
311|- 쿠아아아악!
312|
313|- 크아아아!
314|
315|푸른 겁화가 기둥이 되어 솟구치고, 꺼지지 않는 불길에 휩싸인 몬스터들이 비명을 지른다.
316|
317|그리고 이내 아무것도 들리지 않게 되었을 때, 나는 문득 제자리에 멈춰섰다.
318|
319|“헉, 허억.”
320|
321|숨이 가쁘다. 모래를 한 움큼 씹어 삼킨 것처럼 입안이 텁텁했다.
322|
323|나는 잠시 잊고 있었던 피로가 몰려드는 것을 느끼며 주위를 둘러봤다.
324|
325|넓은 대지 위, 서 있는 몬스터는 더 이상 존재하지 않았다.
326|
327|흉성을 토해 내던 오우거와 트롤도, 허공을 배회하던 와이번과 가고일도.
328|
329|그리고…….
330|
331|투둑, 털썩!
332|
333|언데드로 부활한 공안무력부 헌터들도.
334|
335|마지막 사명을 다한 그들은 마치 실이 끊긴 인형처럼 차례차례 쓰러졌다.
336|

[P88]
“Help me fulfill my mission.”

[P89]
“…!”

[P90]
“I swore an oath on the day I became a Hunter. I swore that I would fight monsters until the moment my life ended. That oath still stands.”

[P91]
Lei Fei had already fulfilled his mission. He had charged forward bravely and met a glorious end.

[P92]
When he fought humanity as the Death Knight Lord, he had been acting on the Arch Lich’s will, not his own.

[P93]
And yet he wanted to fight again. Though his life had already ended, he stood tall once more and reaffirmed his mission.

[P94]
That was why I had to ask.

[P95]
“Why? Why go this far?”

[P96]
Lei Fei smiled faintly.

[P97]
“What a foolish question.”

[P98]
“What?”

[P99]
“Why did you come running here alone, knowing that countless monsters and dangers awaited you? Why am I trying to fight until the very end? What’s the difference?”

[P100]
“…!”

[P101]
“You already know the answer. That is all.”

[P102]
I already knew the answer.

[P103]
The moment I heard those words, a shiver ran down my spine.

[P104]
Lei Fei looked at me as I stood speechless, then raised a hand and gestured around us.

[P105]
The countless monsters still remaining on the battlefield were reflected in his eyes, which had already lost the light of life.

[P106]
“This…will be my final battle.”

[P107]
Schlk!

[P108]
Lei Fei pulled White Flame from his chest and handed it to me, then raised his sword.

[P109]
Instead of the dazzling aura blade that symbolized an S-rank Hunter, ominous dark mana coiled around the blade and surged upward.

[P110]
But the one wielding that power was not the Death Knight Lord.

[P111]
He was a Hunter burning through the last of his life to fulfill his mission.

[P112]
“I’d like to fight alongside them. But will they allow me?”

[P113]
Anyone who did not know the circumstances would have dismissed his words as nonsense.

[P114]
But I understood what Lei Fei meant. Lowering White Flame’s spearhead at an angle, I answered.

[P115]
“They’ll be glad. If they’re the people I know.”

[P116]
“…That’s what I thought.”

[P117]
A red light flickered in Lei Fei’s gray-white eyes.

[P118]
The mana he drew out with all his remaining strength seeped across the battlefield. Then a thunderous cry burst from his lips.

[P119]
“Public Security Armed Forces Department—!”

[P120]
And in the next moment—

[P121]
Rustle. Rattle, rattle.

[P122]
At the call of the Death Knight Lord—or rather, the head of the Public Security Armed Forces Department—the hundreds of Hunters who had fallen across the battlefield rose to their feet. Returned from death, they gripped their weapons and assembled in one place.

[P123]
Lei Fei and I stood at their head.

[P124]
“You take the lead. The living must finish this fight.”

[P125]
As though bewitched, I stepped forward.

[P126]
The monster army, thrown into confusion by the unexpected turn of events, finally gathered with savage roars.

[P127]
They came for the commander who had become their enemy.

[P128]
And for me, standing at the front.

[P129]
Step. Step.

[P130]
I walked forward, slowly but firmly.

[P131]
Tap. Tap-tap.

[P132]
Then I gradually picked up speed.

[P133]
Lei Fei and the hundreds of Public Security Armed Forces Department Hunters resurrected as undead followed behind me.

[P134]
It did not take long for the ripples to become a wave and crash over the enemy.

[P135]
At the threshold of what would be their final battle, Lei Fei shouted at the top of his lungs.

[P136]
“Wipe them all out!”

[P137]
It was the same cry that had echoed through the footage.

[P138]
The Five-Starred Red Flag—their symbol and their pride—shone in the setting sun upon their battered, filthy armor.

[P139]
With my chest throbbing, I became a streak of light and shot toward the monsters.

[P140]
Whoooooosh! KRA-DOOM!

[P141]
* * *

[P142]
Crunch!

[P143]
How many had I brought down by now?

[P144]
Hundreds? A thousand?

[P145]
Slash! Boom!

[P146]
I had no idea. Like a man possessed, I kept moving forward. I smashed, cut, stabbed, and blew apart everything that stood in my way.

[P147]
Whoooooosh!

[P148]
—Kuaaaargh!

[P149]
—Kraaah!

[P150]
Blue hellfire surged upward in pillars, and monsters engulfed in flames that would not go out screamed.

[P151]
Then, when I could no longer hear anything, I suddenly stopped.

[P152]
“Hah, huff.”

[P153]
I was out of breath. My mouth felt rough and dry, as if I had chewed and swallowed a handful of sand.

[P154]
The fatigue I had briefly forgotten came crashing back over me as I looked around.

[P155]
Across the vast expanse of land, not a single monster remained standing.

[P156]
Neither the ogres and Trolls that had bellowed their savage cries nor the Wyverns and Gargoyles that had circled overhead.

[P157]
And…

[P158]
Thud. Thump!

[P159]
The Public Security Armed Forces Department Hunters resurrected as undead began to fall as well.

[P160]
Having fulfilled their final mission, they collapsed one after another like puppets whose strings had been cut.

[P161]
As I watched them with an emotion I could not put into words, I realized what their collapse meant.

[P162]
“…Lei Fei!”

[P163]
He sat in the middle of the silent battlefield. One arm had been severed and his side torn open, yet he waited for me with a peaceful expression.

[P164]
“You came at just the right time.”

[P165]
I did not know why, but those simple words made something surge up inside my chest.

[P166]
We had not even known each other for ten years, yet a curse slipped from my lips before I could stop it.

[P167]
“Damn it…”

[P168]
“Don’t swear so much. I saw you on television, and it seems to be a habit. Women won’t like that, and it’s not good for children’s education.”

[P169]
Lei Fei let out a quiet laugh. He already knew who I was.

[P170]
“Is that really the problem right now? There has to be some way…”

[P171]
—There is no such way, you treacherous human.

[P172]
The Skeleton Warlord’s voice was deeper and more subdued than usual.

[P173]
Lei Fei stared at him, eyes widening.

[P174]
“A monster?”

[P175]
—I am a commander, foolish but somewhat remarkable human.

[P176]
“A monster, then. I have no idea what’s going on, but…yes, if you’re Jin Taekyung, I’m sure you’ll handle it somehow.”

[P177]
Lei Fei nodded and raised his head toward the sky. His slowly blinking gray-white eyes reflected the sky, now stained entirely red.

[P178]
“Could you pass along one message?”

[P179]
I did not ask the foolish question, *To whom?*

[P180]
I already knew.

[P181]
“Tell them I love them. And tell them I’m sorry I couldn’t come home.”

[P182]
It was the final message a dead man left for his family.

[P183]
My chest churning, I answered.

[P184]
“…I will.”

[P185]
“Thank you. You’re a good person.”

[P186]
Lei Fei smiled faintly and tapped my shoulder with his one remaining hand.

[P187]
With a dry, crumbling sound, his fingers broke apart into dust. Then his arm, his leg, his chest…

[P188]
At the very end, one last sentence slipped between his lips.

[P189]
“Go west. End this war.”

[P190]
Whoooooosh.

[P191]

[P192]

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

Crunch!

Whoooooosh!

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.
